title: Raise the Theatre Curtain!
summary: Practise the parts of a Spanish play script, including dialogue and stage directions.
keyIdeas: In plays, characters communicate through dialogue and actions.
Stage directions guide gestures and movements. In these scripts, they appear in brackets.
Plays can be organised into acts and scenes.

activities.prompt: What are the stage directions in brackets in a play script used for?
activities.explanation: Stage directions tell actors how to move or express themselves on stage.
activities.hint: Look at the notes in brackets in the script.
options: They describe actors' gestures, movements or tone of voice.
They are lines the actors must shout very loudly.
They contain the names of the audience members.

activities.prompt: In a play, a narrator always tells us everything the characters do.
activities.explanation: False. A play can show its story through characters' dialogue and actions without a narrator.

activities.prompt: This script divides scenes when characters enter or leave. Complete the Spanish sentence.
activities.explanation: In this common way of organising a script, entrances and exits mark the scene divisions.
activities.sentence: En este guion, cada entrada o salida de un personaje inicia una nueva ___.

activities.prompt: Match each theatre term with its main role.
activities.explanation: People and resources have different roles in preparing a theatre performance.

pairs.right: Writes the text of the play.
Guides the actors and organises the production.
Decorates the stage and creates its setting.
Conversation between two or more characters.

activities.prompt: Sort each Spanish fragment into Dialogue or Stage Direction.
activities.explanation: Dialogue contains the words actors say. The stage directions here describe actions in brackets.

items.text: ¡Rápido, esconde la llave en el cofre!
(Señala hacia la ventana con ojos asustados)
¿Quién ha encendido la luz del pasillo?
(Sale de puntillas por la puerta izquierda)
Buenos días a todos los viajeros.
(Baja la voz y mira fijamente el reloj)

activities.prompt: Read this Spanish school play extract and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: A play script gives information through both spoken words and stage directions.
activities.title: El mapa del desván
activities.text:
(Entran Lucía y Omar al desván a oscuras. Omar lleva una linterna parpadeante).
LUCÍA: (Temblando) Hace mucho frío aquí arriba, Omar. ¿Seguro que el abuelo guardó el mapa en este baúl?
OMAR: (Abriendo la tapa con esfuerzo) ¡Completamente seguro! Mira, entre estos periódicos viejos... ¡aquí está!
LUCÍA: (Da un salto de alegría) ¡Lo encontramos! Pero espera... ¿qué significa esa cruz roja junto al molino?
OMAR: (Mira el dibujo muy pensativo) Es el escondite secreto. ¡Rápido, vamos al jardín antes de que anochezca!
(Los dos niños salen corriendo mientras baja lentamente el telón).

questions.prompt: What does Omar carry to light up the attic?
questions.explanation: The first stage direction says Omar carries a flickering torch.

questions.prompt: How do we know Lucía feels cold at the start of the scene?
questions.explanation: The stage direction «(Temblando)» tells us that she is shivering.
options: Because Omar offers her a thick blanket.
Because a narrator says so through a microphone.
From the stage direction saying she is shivering.

activities.prompt: Put the class's steps for preparing their play in order.
activities.explanation: First assign the parts, then rehearse, prepare the stage and costumes, and finally perform.
items: Assign the characters' parts in the script.
Rehearse the dialogue and movements on stage.
Set up the scenery and put on the costumes.
Perform the play in front of the audience.

activities.prompt: During rehearsal, Wei says this aloud: «Abriendo los brazos, ¡qué alegría verte!». What mistake did he make?
activities.explanation: «Abriendo los brazos» is a stage direction describing an action. The actor should perform it rather than say it to the audience.
activities.hint: Which part of the script should be acted rather than spoken?
options: He spoke too quickly during the scene.
He forgot to say his character's dialogue.
He read aloud the stage direction he should have acted.

activities.prompt: During a performance, the curtain falls and the scenery changes from a forest to a royal palace. Which main part of the play has ended?
activities.explanation: Acts are major divisions of a play. They are often separated by the curtain falling.
activities.hint: Choose the major division of a play.

activities.prompt: The detective looks for a clue without attracting attention. Choose the suitable Spanish stage direction.
activities.explanation: Whispering and looking around fit a detective trying not to attract attention.
activities.sentence: DETECTIVE: ___ ¡He encontrado la huella misteriosa detrás del cuadro!
